title: Ripple scenario result
description: The answer. Produced by web/lib/simulate.ts in the browser and by model/ripple_model/simulate.py as the reference; the parity test asserts both agree. Every quantity a user sees is an interval, never a bare point.

interval.description: Posterior summary of one quantity. p05/p95 are the 90% interval the UI must always show next to the mean.

band.description: One week of a fan chart: median line plus the 50% and 90% bands.

money.description: Units, revenue and profit for the same object.

scenario.description: Echo of the scenario that produced this result (contract/scenario.schema.json).

baseline.description: Totals over the horizon with no change.

with_change.description: Totals over the horizon with the change.

incremental.description: with_change minus baseline, differenced WITHIN each posterior draw before summarizing — this is the headline, and the only honest way to get the interval.

p_profit_positive.description: Share of draws where incremental profit > 0. The 'chance it pays' number.

break_even.description: Optional: where the change stops paying, for the UI hint line.

value.description: Largest discount / price change / fixed cost that still keeps P(profit > 0) >= 0.5. null when it pays nowhere in range.

weekly.description: Fan chart data, one entry per horizon week, in order.

week.description: 0-based offset from the start of the horizon.

t.description: Absolute week index used by season(), i.e. meta.weeks + week.

week_start.description: ISO date, when the caller knows the calendar.

promo_active.description: Shades the promo weeks on the chart.

dip_active.description: True on the week right after a promo week, where b_dip bites.

segments.description: Incremental effect per segment, for the segment bars. Empty when meta.has_segments is false.

share_of_total.description: Share of total incremental units; may be negative if the segment loses.

cities.description: Incremental effect per city. For new_city there is a single entry with the candidate's name.

extrapolation.description: new_city with a standardized trait outside the training range.

no_price_variation.description: The fitted data never varied price, so elasticity is prior-driven. The UI must say so.

warnings.description: Short sentences to show above the chart.

source.description: Which implementation produced it — used by the parity test report.

net_price.description: Price actually charged under the change (promo/price types).
